certifications.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert
certifications.subtitle: Subject matter expertise in designing cloud and hybrid solutions that run on Azure
certifications.description: This certification is for candidates with advanced experience and knowledge of IT operations, including networking, virtualization, identity, security, business continuity, disaster recovery, data platforms, and governance.
certifications.fullDescription: As a Microsoft Azure solutions architect, you have subject matter expertise in designing cloud and hybrid solutions that run on Azure, including compute, network, storage, monitoring, and security. Your responsibilities include advising stakeholders and translating business requirements into designs for Azure solutions that align with the Azure Well-Architected Framework and Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. In this role, you implement solutions on Azure by partnering with various other job roles, including developers, administrators, security engineers, and data engineers. Candidates should have advanced experience and knowledge of IT operations, including networking, virtualization, identity, security, business continuity, disaster recovery, data platforms, and governance, and manage how decisions in each area affect an overall solution. Additionally, candidates should have experience with Azure administration, Azure development, and DevOps processes. The English language version of this certification was updated on October 18, 2024.

certifications.title: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
certifications.subtitle: Competence in Kubernetes administration in a hands-on environment
certifications.description: The CKA program provides assurance that Certified Kubernetes Administrators have the skills, knowledge, and competency to perform the responsibilities of Kubernetes administrators.
certifications.fullDescription: The Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) program, created by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) in collaboration with The Linux Foundation, aims to develop the Kubernetes ecosystem by certifying administrators. It is an online, proctored, performance-based test requiring solving multiple issues from a command line, separate from the Kubernetes Certified Service Provider (KCSP) program. CNCF has open-sourced the curriculum for training companies, and offers wholesale pricing on exams for bulk purchases by training partners.

certifications.title: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect
certifications.subtitle: Enable organizations to leverage Google Cloud technologies
certifications.description: The Professional Cloud Architect certification assesses the ability to design, develop, and manage robust, secure, scalable, efficient, cost-effective, highly available, and flexible cloud solutions to drive business objectives.
certifications.fullDescription: Professional Cloud Architects enable organizations to leverage Google Cloud technologies. With a thorough understanding of cloud architecture and Google Cloud, they design, develop, and manage robust, secure, scalable, efficient, cost-effective, highly available, and flexible solutions to drive business objectives. The certification exam assesses the ability to: design and plan a cloud solution architecture; manage and provision the cloud solution infrastructure; design for security and compliance; analyze and optimize technical and business processes; manage implementations of cloud architecture; ensure solution and operations reliability. The upcoming version of the exam, live in English on October 30, highlights the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework and includes new case studies focusing on generative AI technology.

certifications.title: CompTIA Security+
certifications.subtitle: Premier global certification for core security functions
certifications.description: CompTIA Security+ is the premier global certification that establishes the essential skills required for core security functions and a career in IT security.
certifications.fullDescription: CompTIA Security+ is the most widely recognized credential, invaluable for advancing in the dynamic field of cybersecurity. It establishes essential skills for core security functions, focusing on securing networks, applications, and devices, and ensuring data integrity, confidentiality, and availability through practical, hands-on skills.

domains.name: General Security Concepts
domains.description: Covers security controls, fundamental concepts, change management, and cryptographic solutions
topics: Comparing technical, preventive, managerial, deterrent, operational, detective, physical, corrective, compensating, and directive controls
Summarizing confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA), non-repudiation, authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA), zero trust, and deception/disruption technology
Explaining business processes, technical implications, documentation, and version control
Using public key infrastructure (PKI), encryption, obfuscation, hashing, digital signatures, and blockchain

domains.name: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations
domains.description: Focuses on threat actors, vectors, attack surfaces, vulnerabilities, malicious activity, and mitigation techniques
topics: Comparing nation-states, unskilled attackers, hacktivists, insider threats, organized crime, shadow IT, and motivations like data exfiltration, espionage, and financial gain
Explaining message-based, unsecure networks, social engineering, file-based, voice call, supply chain, and vulnerable software vectors
Explaining application, hardware, mobile device, virtualization, operating system (OS)-based, cloud-specific, web-based, and supply chain vulnerabilities
Analyzing malware attacks, password attacks, application attacks, physical attacks, network attacks, and cryptographic attacks
Using segmentation, access control, configuration enforcement, hardening, isolation, and patching

domains.name: Security Architecture
domains.description: Covers architecture models, enterprise infrastructure, data protection, and resilience and recovery
topics: Comparing on-premises, cloud, virtualization, Internet of Things (IoT), industrial control systems (ICS), and infrastructure as code (IaC)
Applying security principles to infrastructure considerations, control selection, and secure communication/access
Comparing data types, securing methods, general considerations, and classifications
Explaining high availability, site considerations, testing, power, platform diversity, backups, and continuity of operations

domains.name: Security Operations
domains.description: Includes computing resources, asset management, vulnerability management, alerting and monitoring, enterprise security, identity and access management, automation and orchestration, incident response, and data sources
topics: Applying secure baselines, mobile solutions, hardening, wireless security, application security, sandboxing, and monitoring
Explaining acquisition, disposal, assignment, and monitoring/tracking of hardware, software, and data assets
Identifying, analyzing, remediating, validating, and reporting vulnerabilities
Explaining monitoring tools and computing resource activities
Modifying firewalls, IDS/IPS, DNS filtering, DLP, NAC, and EDR/XDR
Implementing provisioning, SSO, MFA, and privileged access tools
Explaining automation use cases, scripting benefits, and considerations
Implementing processes, training, testing, root cause analysis, threat hunting, and digital forensics
Using log data and other sources to support investigations

domains.name: Security Program Management and Oversight

Explaining risk identification, calculation, prioritization, and reporting
Applying risk treatment, transfer, acceptance, and avoidance strategies
Explaining vendor assessment, supply chain assessment, and hardware/software validation
Summarizing data types, classifications, and protection strategies
Explaining compliance frameworks, reporting, and audits/assessments
Implementing security awareness practices and training programs
